cells.tense: The pen is in your hand right now on this half-lit stretch.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: When a jumble is live among others and you already see its shape, say that shape plainly, once, out loud, before anyone has to ask.
cells.core:
You can hold several true things at the same time, and out here the way only ever shows the next step. That combination is not a flaw to fix. It is what lets you walk when the whole route is not visible, and it lets the people beside you walk too.

What wants feeding is the stating. When a jumble is live among others and you already see its shape, say the shape plainly once, before anyone has had to ask. Then let it stand. You do not owe a defense of that frame afterward. The ones with you get something clear to think with instead of fog. Say it first, once, and the next step shows itself.
cells.sheetLine: Say the shape of it once, before anyone asks.
cells.place: where the road shows only the next step

cells.tense: You are bracing at a road you can't write in yet.
cells.act: face one way for three days
cells.ask: Name a muddle you keep turning over, choose the way you'd have it go, and hold that heading three days without re-surveying.
cells.core:
Out here, you are carrying what feels like every truth at once, and the mind keeps bracing for a future it cannot write. So many sides are visible that no heading gets chosen, and the not-choosing starts to feel like the only safe place. It is not safe. It is just tiring, and the way stays dark because nothing is being steered.

What you want is one direction, even a small one. Take something you keep turning over, name how you want it to go, and hold that heading three days without checking everything again. You do not have to be right. You only have to stop surveying long enough for the next step to show. The direction may look silly. Hold it anyway. Radiance comes back through moving one way, not through seeing all ways.
cells.sheetLine: Stop surveying. Hold one heading for three days.
cells.place: where the road shows only the next step

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: join someone in the work so the two streams run as one
cells.ask: Ask someone to work on a real thing alongside you this week, and do it together rather than alone.
cells.core:
You are looking at the muddle from behind, still measuring what it would have shown. Several sides come clear to you at once, but none of them is landing on anything new, because you are not quite present to the work at hand. From outside it reads as patience. From your chair it is more like waiting at a door that is already shut behind you.

The way through is not forcing yourself to be comfortable with not-knowing. That rarely works. It is joining someone in actual work, so the two of you run as one flow for a while. Then what you perceive comes out of the doing, not out of trying to see it. Choose one real thing, ask someone to do it with you, and go. What comes next shows itself once you are moving with another, not before.
cells.sheetLine: Join someone in real work and go with them.
cells.place: where the road shows only the next step

cells.tense: You are holding more truth than you know you are holding.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Find a fair move nobody would check, decide it by your own sense of what's right, and do it this week without telling a soul.
cells.core:
You keep handling the muddle with people better than you give yourself credit for. Several sides come clear to you at once — that is your way — and quietly you have been trading on it, weighing things, sorting what is fair, and calling it the cost of being present. The muddle clears around you and you say it just happened.

That weighing is yours. The move is small. Do one fair thing this week where no one is watching — one little case, decided by your own sense of what is right, not by any reckoning. Return what you owe before anyone asks. Not for credit, not to be seen. That is what your conscience does when you let it, and you are already doing it. Do one on purpose, and the one doing it shows up.
cells.sheetLine: Do one fair thing this week where no one will see.
cells.place: where the road shows only the next step
